title: Trying to recall other early pianists: Fred Washington, Black Pete, Coochie Martin
summary: Barnes struggles to remember names of old-time pianists and drummers; the interviewers prompt with Fred Washington and Black Pete.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Frank Henia. Well I'll tell you a little bit.
Well I was a musician by the right name, it's hard for me to tell.
You called him George, let me see, George Piano Player? I can't think. I think now, George Piano Player. Oh boy. Well let's see.
You remember Fred Washington, I have to keep him to mind.
Fred Washington was in the tune. But see Fred was more uptown. Uptown, he played in the district too I know. Yeah, district.
There was another fellow that Bunk used to tell me about, that played with Big Eye in the district. They called him Black Pete. I don't know his real name. Black Pete.

I can't think of Black Pete. We had another one here, with a big thing around here. Not Coochie Martin, that was the drummer too, Coochie Martin. Yeah nobody got a name. But it was, oh that's simple, I can't call that man's name now.
I guess some of the bands didn't use piano, we don't hear much about the old time pianists usually.
No, well Lewis, we had a piano player, Lewis what? I don't know. He used to be with us. Not Steve Lewis, no. Steve Lewis, no not Steve, not Steve, another Lewis.
